Oct 23 : Oil prices were little changed in early Asian trade on Friday, after rising 4 per cent to a five-month high in the previous session due to concern of further energy supply disruption after Houthi attacks on top exporter Saudi Arabia. Brent crude futures was down 21 cents, or 0.2 per cent, at $112.96 a barrel as of 0030 GMT, while US West Texas Intermediate crude was down 27 cents, or 0.3 per cent, at $98.12. On a weekly basis, WTI was on track to end two weeks of gain to finish lower. Brent, which settled at its highest since May 4 on Thursday, is set to close higher for the third successive week. Saudi Aramco on Thursday ordered the evacuation of its headquarters in Dhahran on the Gulf near Bahrain, Reuters reported, as fighting intensified between the world's largest crude exporter and Yemen-based Houthis.

Clashes between the Houthis and a Saudi-led coalition that backs Yemen's internationally recognised government have raged since the Iran-aligned Houthis pushed towards Bab el-Mandeb, a shipping chokepoint at the mouth of the Red Sea. In Libya, an oil pipeline valve from the Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port has been shut, leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the National Oil Corporation told Reuters on Thursday. Separately, Russia said on Wednesday it was ready to resume US-mediated talks with Ukraine next month, after President Vladimir Putin hosted US envoy Steve Witkoff for talks in St Petersburg. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he hoped negotiations, which would be the first since February, will take place early in November. Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, US energy data showed. Sanctions aimed at keeping Russian energy out of global markets after Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 have pushed up oil prices.

SEOUL, Oct 23 : HD Hyundai Co said on Friday it has signed a deal with Kiewit Corp to start building an advanced US shipyard next year, with operations expected to begin in 2029 and create about 3,000 domestic jobs. The new shipyard is expected to boost US shipbuilding capacity and help revive the industry, Hyundai said. The partners will explore opportunities in both commercial ships and military support vessels, it said in a statement.  • South Korea pledged to invest $150 billion in the US shipbuilding sector, as part of $350 billion of investment funds the Asian country agreed to put into US projects in return for winning U.S. tariff cuts in last year. • Construction of the shipyard will begin in 2027 and the two companies will also set up a joint venture. • The joint venture will explore building US navy support vessels, commercial ship opportunities, and supplying ship blocks and modules to US shipyards. • HD Hyundai said the new shipyard is expected to revive the US shipbuilding industry and expand Korea-US shipbuilding cooperation.

FAST

Oct 22 : Microsoft researchers say an AI tool that diagnoses patients step by step, as doctors do, was more than twice as accurate as general physicians at solving complex medical cases, according to a study published on Thursday in Science. The model identifies and coordinates the questions that should be asked of a patient, as well as the exams and tests that should be ordered, using an "orchestrator" that organizes how AI will tackle a problem by employing a simulated panel of clinical experts collaborating to solve diagnostic cases, according to the report. Existing medical AI models typically take an all-at-once approach that examines all of a patient's symptoms, lab results and imaging studies to generate a diagnosis. With the orchestrator coordinating the steps to reaching a diagnosis, the AI model first decides what to ask about the patient’s history and what is significant in the physical exam. Based on what it learns, it decides which tests to order, considers the results, and orders further testing as appropriate.

All the while, it is updating its working hypotheses and plans, the research leaders said in an interview. Tasked with diagnosing more than 300 highly unusual and confusing medical dilemmas, the model employing the diagnostic orchestrator was more than twice as accurate at "working up" the patient and determining the diagnosis as general physicians using textbooks and the internet. The tool also outperformed human physicians when presented with scenarios drawn from a major database of emergency room admissions. Assessments comparing these types of older systems to human doctors usually use multiple-choice questions, the researchers said. "AI has become very good at getting a 100 per cent pass rate on those,” said Dr. Dominic King, the corporate vice president of the health unit at Microsoft AI, whose team is developing the new technology. “But of course, that's not real-world. No patient ever came to see me with a nice summary.” The researchers also found that diagnostic processes cost less when the orchestrator designs the work-ups than when human doctors do. “We're not just measuring the accuracy of the systems. We're also measuring how judiciously and carefully it goes through a diagnostic work-up,” said Harsha Nori, head of AI at Microsoft AI Health. In a collaboration with Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center in Boston, the researchers will next test the tool’s ability to triage patients in emergency department waiting rooms.

Source: Reuters

TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan's manufacturing sector expanded at its slowest pace in seven months in October as output and new order growth eased, a business survey showed on Friday. • The flash S&P Global Japan Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) fell to 53.3 in October from 54.1 in September. A reading above 50.0 indicates expansion in activity, while below that level signals contraction • New orders of goods producers rose at the weakest pace since March, while new export business across Japan's private sector increased at the softest rate in four months • Manufacturers logged the weakest rise in output since March, while goods producers recorded the slowest increase in new orders since March, the survey showed

The flash S&P Global Japan Services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 52.0 from 51.3, with the survey showing a stronger increase in business activity and faster sales growth • At the broader economy level, the S&P Global Flash Japan Composite PMI Output Index was unchanged at 52.3, marking a 19th straight month of expansion in private sector activity • "The October flash PMI data indicated that overall business activity growth across Japan was unchanged from a month prior to remain weaker than the average for the year-to-date," said Usamah Bhatti, economist at S&P Global Market Intelligence • Across the private sector, new business rose at the slowest pace in three months and export business growth eased to a four-month low. TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan has yet to see conditions met for the government to officially declare an end to deflation, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said on Friday. The government's decision on whether to declare an end to deflation will take into account various factors to ensure Japan will not revert to periods of persistent price falls, Kiuchi told a press conference. TOKYO, Oct 23 : Japan's annual core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's 2 per cent target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike. The figures underscored how higher fuel costs from the prolonged Middle East conflict, elevated import prices driven by the weak yen and price pressures from robust AI demand were blunting the impact of government fuel subsidies. Having just raised interest rates last month, the Bank of Japan is set to stand pat on policy next week but may revise up its inflation forecast and signal its readiness to keep pushing up still-low borrowing costs, sources have told Reuters. The core consumer price index (CPI), which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1 per cent in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast. It followed a 1.7 per cent rise in August.

The BOJ raised its key rate to a 31-year high of 1.25 per cent last month, signalling a shift to guarding against underlying inflation overshooting its target and raising the prospect of additional rate hikes. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda has warned that underlying inflation, or the broad price trend stripping away temporary, one-off factors, may overshoot its 2 per cent target on price pressures from the Middle East conflict, a weak yen and brisk AI demand.

(Refiles to add dropped words "unsolicited links" in SCAMMERS section) By AJ Vicens Oct 22 : Much of the world woke Wednesday to news that PHP, a coding language most people have never heard of but that underlies roughly 70 per cent of all websites, had a hackable vulnerability, sending businesses and governments scrambling to fix it. While the PHP glitches sit in the underlying code itself, the NSA warned that attackers could use them to take control of web servers to steal data, disrupt services or move through networks on services the average person relies on every day.

Experts say responsibility mostly lies with software providers and organizations that serve customers. But there are basic steps everyone should take to protect themselves.  USE MULTI-FACTOR AUTHENTIFICATION MFA, or multi-factor authentication, requires two forms of verification to access a protected site, such as a password plus a text-based code or security key. Emily Austin, principal security researcher at cybersecurity firm Censys, recommended unique passwords for individual websites, and for people to monitor any transactions. “But realistically, for situations like the PHP vulnerabilities, there really isn’t much an end user can do beyond hope the services they rely on either don’t use PHP or have people actively working on patching,” Austin said. The PHP flaws are the latest in a series of severe software bugs made worse by increasingly capable and accessible large language models. Long-hidden flaws in widely used software, once too obscure or complex for humans to exploit, are now much easier to surface and weaponize. MAKE HARDWARE UPDATES AUTOMATIC Dan Guido, CEO and co-founder of cybersecurity firm Trail of Bits, recommended people “turn on automatic updates for your phone, computer, and home router.” Companies typically issue security updates when patches are available for known vulnerabilities, so installing them promptly limits the window for bad actors.  Even so, consumers remain at the mercy of the services they rely on, Guido said. “Someone visiting a website can do everything right, like use two-factor authentication, and still have their information exposed,” Guido said. “You can't patch your hospital's website.”  Most of the work falls on companies running services, Guido said. “They need to deploy fixes faster and limit the damage that compromised systems can cause.” Runa Sandvik, the founder of Granitt and a digital security expert, said people need to update apps and services on their devices whenever they're available, and to not forget about internet-connected devices around the house. "I can see a scenario in which some people have some sort of IoT device at home that maybe doesn't get frequent updates, maybe doesn't get any updates at all," Sandvik said. "It's worth double checking with the vendor to see if there is anything available." PATCH, PATCH, PATCH Dr. Daniel Gardham, a lecturer at the Surrey Centre for Cyber Security and the University of Surrey, said organizations must know what software they run, patch promptly and check whether they've already been compromised. In the AI age, attackers have the advantage, Gardham added. “Finding vulnerabilities is becoming faster and easier, but fixing them across the range of systems that rely on this software is much harder,” Gardham said. “How well organizations manage that gap will determine whether AI makes the internet safer or more vulnerable.”  BEWARE OF SCAMMERS Any time a major cybersecurity threat makes the news, scammers and cybercriminals will try to take advantage, said Nic Adams, co-founder and CEO of 0rcus, a cyberkinetics company. Be wary of unsolicited links. "When these headlines hit, check the affected company's instructions by opening its app or typing its website address yourself," Adams said. "An urgent message telling you to 'secure your account' deserves extra scrutiny."  YOUR MONEY IS SAFE Banks have been preparing for this moment since frontier models came out, and have "worked extremely hard to ensure there is no more low-hanging fruit for the bad guys to go after," said Paul Benda, executive vice president of risk, fraud and cybersecurity at the American Bankers Association.  However, Benda added, "we are in a new normal" in terms of cyber threats, and consumers need to be aware, especially in the wake of the PHP vulnerabilities, when shopping with random retailers or websites "where their security is not going to be as good as your bank."  Benda said consumers should not reuse passwords across shopping sites, and should consider using passkeys where possible, which are digital keys specific to certain websites, that avoid the need to enter a password into a website and a phishing resistant.

Source: Reuters

SEOUL, Oct 23 : South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix said on Friday that it had suspended its review of a US initial public offering for its Solidigm subsidiary, citing financial market volatility and share price trends. South Korea's financial regulator said earlier this week that the listing could run afoul of the country's dual-listing restrictions, which were tightened in July to strengthen shareholder protection. SK Hynix said in a statement it would continue to explore ways to fund Solidigm's expansion and enhance shareholder value, including reviewing the timing, scale and financing of future investments. "This decision does not reflect any change in Solidigm's growth prospects or investment needs," the company said.

The move brings an end, at least for now, to a potential fundraising option that Reuters reported could raise as much as $15 billion, highlighting the challenge of balancing investment needs driven by booming AI-related memory demand with growing concerns in South Korea over the impact of subsidiary listings on existing shareholders. Despite strong business performance at both SK Hynix and Solidigm, the company said increased market volatility and a broader correction in semiconductor stocks had prompted it to reconsider the listing. Shares in SK Hynix have fallen more than 30 per cent since the potential Solidigm IPO was reported in late September, compared with a 20 per cent decline in South Korea's benchmark KOSPI index over the same period. The announcement could, however, help improve investor sentiment towards semiconductor stocks, said Han Ji-young, an analyst at Kiwoom Securities. Concerns over Meta's creditworthiness, a selloff in US AI stocks and pressure from oil prices had repeatedly weighed on markets, eroding investor confidence, he added. GROWING SCRUTINY OVER DUAL LISTINGS The decision also follows heightened regulatory scrutiny of the proposed listing. Financial Supervisory Service Governor Lee Chan-jin told a parliamentary hearing earlier this week that regulators were examining whether Solidigm's potential US initial public offering would require a review under domestic rules. Solidigm, based in Rancho Cordova, California, is SK Hynix's US subsidiary specialising in NAND flash memory and solid-state drives. SK Hynix had considered an IPO as one of several ways to finance Solidigm's expansion amid growing demand for memory chips driven by artificial intelligence. The company said raising external capital through a listing could have boosted its cash flow, helping fund new production facilities while supporting shareholder returns through dividends, share buybacks and share cancellations. It added that an IPO could have helped investors better recognise Solidigm's growth potential, which it said was not fully reflected in the parent company's valuation. Shares of SK Hynix were down 1.3 per cent in morning trade, compared with a 2.3 per cent decline in the benchmark KOSPI.

WASHINGTON, Oct 22 : The Federal Communications Commission said on Thursday it has granted a waiver to Intel from its ban on some foreign-made advanced robotics. The FCC said it would grant a one-year waiver of its rules in order to prevent "potential disruptions in the availability of domestic semiconductor manufacturing services for Intel’s customers." Intel in a petition last week said the robotic devices are critical to its US semiconductor manufacturing. Without the waiver, Intel would not have been allowed to make software, firmware, and hardware changes for its "Automated Guided Vehicles" that it said could be classified by the agency as robots. Intel told the FCC there is a lack of proven domestic alternatives that meet operational requirements and replacing the automated guided vehicles would take Intel years and could disrupt its manufacturing operations.

NEW YORK, Oct 22 : The tab for the next round of the AI buildout came due on Thursday. Investors sold shares of Meta Platforms and a wealth of companies central to the AI trade, a day after Meta — one of the hyperscalers spending billions to build data centers and other infrastructure supporting the AI boom — said it would issue a new class of shares that will help it raise funds.  Meta fell 7 per cent, its largest drop since July. SpaceX declined 9 per cent and semiconductor company Nvidia — a bellwether of the AI trade — dropped 4 per cent. The Nasdaq Composite lost 2.6 per cent, its largest decline since June 5.  Sentiment was also hurt by a 12 per cent plunge in shares of semiconductor company Lam Research following its results. The Philadelphia Semiconductor index lost 6.7 per cent.

The pullback is the latest test for the AI trade as investors focus on the rising costs of long-term projects where the payoff remains uncertain. Tech firms have borrowed huge sums over the past year for AI spending, but Wall Street now expects that the rise in borrowing costs will motivate tech companies like Meta to sell billions of dollars in stock to fund the next round of building. That dilution could put pressure on share prices, and is a potentially unwelcome development when major US stock indexes remain near all-time highs despite a punishing month of volatile trading. RETURN ON INVESTMENT CONCERNS Selling started with "the big question about the (return on investment) on all the spending," said Matthew Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak. "It's just becoming more and more evident to people that it's going to take a lot longer."  Thomas Hayes, chairman at Great Hill Capital LLC in New York, agreed that ROI concerns are central while also citing remarks by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang about a financing bottleneck for smaller AI companies as contributing to the selling.  Meta said on Wednesday it would use new Class C shares, which hold no voting power, to fund AI spending and other priorities. Meta also raised the low end of its annual spending forecast to $135 billion from $130 billion, with the high end unchanged at $145 billion. That level of spending will require lots of investor participation in coming stock sales. Meta reported negative free cash flow of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, compared with positive free cash flow of $10.63 billion a year earlier. It was the first cash burn at Meta in more than a decade. “More spending, negative free cash flow, not enough revenue being generated from the spend (is) concerning investors that this is just sort of a bit of a money pit,” said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield, Connecticut. The action highlights concern over how AI investment will be paid for. Credit default swaps, which track perceived default risk for the debt of the biggest AI players, have largely risen over the past year, with Meta’s hitting a record on Thursday. INVESTOR ANXIETY SHOWS Fresh signs of market anxiety over AI spending snowballed into a broad market selloff Thursday, with some saying an AI pullback could hit US growth. Investors sought the safety of Treasury bonds, sending those prices higher. "This is your classic rotation day,” said Joe Saluzzi, partner, co-founder and co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. “You can see the money going into Treasuries, so it's a classic safety move ... They are rotating out of techs, out of the AIs, and into the more safety trades, whether it's bonds or some of those big Dow Jones stocks.” Thursday’s selloff added to the pressure on the neocloud companies at the heart of the AI buildout, with Nebius off 7 per cent after announcing a new $3.5 billion credit line from Citigroup and CoreWeave, whose unsecured bond yields soared to 15 per cent in last week’s AI selloff, down 10 per cent. Bank of America analyst Tal Liani said in a report on Thursday he is maintaining a buy rating and a price target of $140 on CoreWeave stock heading into next month’s earnings report, though he said he believes the firm will need to raise $20 billion to fund commitments to customers — the sort of prospect that is generating anxiety among tech investors.  "Nobody is worried about Meta or Amazon or Google getting the financing they need," Maley said. "But if it gets prohibitive for smaller companies, then you don't have to have an implosion of things to make people nervous."

Source: Reuters

Oct 22 : AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier this year. The exercise, conducted from July 21 to August 11, gave outside researchers "a deep level of access" to OpenAI's internal infrastructure for so-called embedded evaluations, the safety nonprofits said on Thursday. METR and Redwood said they each sent one researcher, tested an arrangement giving access to OpenAI's internal code, documentation and some technical staff. Both were accompanied on site and used OpenAI-issued devices that "never left the premises". OpenAI told the safety organizations it has since patched all vulnerabilities affecting its production safeguards, although METR and Redwood said they had not verified the fixes.

AI labs, experts and the Trump administration have touted independent evaluation by outside reviewers as a way to safely advance the technology without slowing its development. While OpenAI received a full 61-page internal report, METR and Redwood said they agreed to publish only a broad summary publicly, and gave OpenAI the right to redact sensitive information. Unlike in some previous evaluations, they could not independently disclose those redactions, but said they expected greater transparency in future evaluations. The researchers also identified a potential way for OpenAI's Codex agents to bypass security restrictions and act with their users' full permissions. The evaluators assessed the monitoring system as it existed on and before July 21, and noted that OpenAI was expanding the system during the exercise. Oct 22 : Cable production capacity is emerging as a bottleneck for AI-driven data centre construction, Nexans' finance chief said, as demand rises faster than the industry's ability to expand manufacturing capacity. Global cable capacity is tight and building a new cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable production line, known in the industry as a CV line, takes around three years, limiting how quickly suppliers can respond to demand, Nexans CFO Vincent Piquet told Reuters. "Things can't move quickly and the people building these data centres are in a great hurry," Piquet said. Data centres require large amounts of low- and medium-voltage cable to connect power infrastructure, with larger facilities consuming proportionately more medium-voltage cable.

The strain on power infrastructure is already delaying some projects. In September, Oracle issued a force majeure notice to a Blue Owl unit developing a large data centre in New Mexico, citing potential difficulties securing sufficient power for the site. Piquet said grid constraints, while slowing some projects, were also supporting demand for Nexans' products and allowing the company to be more selective when allocating capacity. French distribution network operator Enedis has moved from annual procurement agreements to contracts lasting six or seven years in order to secure cable supply, he said. While Europe generally faces fewer grid-connection challenges than the United States and benefits from stronger electricity networks in some northern countries, Piquet said lengthy regulatory processes were delaying certain projects. He said he did not expect demand linked to artificial intelligence to slow, although Europe's data-centre expansion was likely to be less pronounced than in the United States because private investment capacity was smaller and public funding played a larger role.

BRUSSELS, Oct 22 : Digital advertisers and publishers lobbied on Thursday for EU and UK regulators to suspend Meta Platforms' new commercial terms due to come into effect on October 30, alleging that these would give Meta an unlimited right to use their content for its AI services. Advocacy group the Movement for an Open Web, whose members include digital advertisers and publishers, said it had complained to the European Commission and the UK's Competition and Markets Authority and requested interim measures. Publishers worldwide are stepping up their fight with AI companies that use their content without permission to train large language models, underscoring the clash between copyright owners and those citing fair use arguments. "Meta's new terms are clearly anti-competitive. Many businesses effectively have no choice but to use Meta's services and these conditions would force them to sign away the rights to their digital content with no means of opting out," Tim Cowen, co-founder of the Movement for an Open Web, said.

Meta said it disagreed with the complaint. "The crawling terms we consolidated only applied to our ads and business products, and we've clarified that in the terms themselves. It does not change how Meta uses web crawlers," a Meta spokesperson said. "As always, content owners can use robots.txt to signal their preferences. This is not about scraping news sites, and these updates don't give us new rights that supersede those preferences." The CMA said it met with Meta on Wednesday to get more details on its new business terms. "This is an important issue and we recognise the concerns that have been raised by businesses in the UK. We are engaged in urgent discussions with Meta as we consider our next steps," a CMA spokesperson said. The European Commission said it has received a complaint which it would assess in line with its usual procedure and that it was committed to ensuring that Meta's practices comply with EU laws.  Companies requesting interim measures have to show that they will suffer serious and irreparable damage from the alleged anti-competitive practices. The criticism by the Movement for an Open Web followed similar complaints aired by the European Publishers Council (EPC) last week and Germany's Digital Publishers and Newspaper Publishers Association (BDZV) and the Association of the Free Press (MVFP) earlier this week.

Oct 22 : Anyone who has watched a manta ray glide over a reef knows how unhurried these marine animals can look. Yet researchers working off Costa Rica found their movements are varied, with juveniles staying nearby and close to shore while adults venture hundreds of kilometres. Manta rays are among the ocean's largest fish, with wing-like fins that can span up to about 8 meters (26 feet) and the largest brain of any fish. Researchers tracked endangered oceanic manta rays between 2018 and 2025, fitting 59 of them with acoustic transmitters and tracking 12 with satellite tags, along with photo identification.  "By combining different technologies ... we were able to piece together a highly detailed map of their movements and their use of coastal cleaning stations," said Jeffry Madrigal-Mesén, director of the research group Mantas Costa Rica and lead author of the study published in the journal Frontiers in Fish Science.

A coastal cleaning station is a rocky reef site where small fish remove parasites from the skin of the manta rays in an example of symbiotic behaviour. Researchers found that smaller, immature mantas stayed within Costa Rica's coastal waters, called its exclusive economic zone. Larger, mature animals undertook long-distance journeys, some reaching as far as the waters off Guatemala. "This makes us believe that smaller mantas do not risk these long migrations, likely due to the threat of large predators like orcas and tiger sharks," Madrigal-Mesén said. The smaller animals in the study measured around 3 to 3.5 meters across (10 to 11.5 feet), compared with around 4 to 4.5 meters (13 to 15 feet) for those making the longer journeys. DANGER FROM PREDATORS A juvenile, at around 3 meters across, would still appear enormous to most swimmers. Yet that size may not be enough protection. Madrigal-Mesén said that "their massive size is one of their main defence mechanisms. It is quite common to see animals missing portions of their bodies, and in many cases, the shape of the wounds strongly suggests they are bites from other large marine predators." What prompts mantas to eventually join the migratory population remains unclear, although researchers suspect that reaching feeding and breeding grounds in highly productive waters across Central America may play a role. The manta rays also repeatedly return to the same coastal cleaning stations. Observations of feeding, courtship and recent mating suggest these sites may also function as social hubs. Scientists do not yet know how mantas navigate back to particular sites. "Based on the bathymetry of the different sites we monitor, there must be a relationship with the rock formations. We humans have favourite places we like to go to," Madrigal-Mesén said. "Why couldn't mantas have a preference for one cleaning station over another?" The findings also suggest the mantas may not roam as far as once thought. Researchers initially suspected that animals seen in Costa Rica might migrate from populations in Ecuador or Mexico. The tracking data instead raises the possibility that Central America has its own distinct population, something the team is now investigating through genetic work. Mantas are particularly vulnerable because, like other rays and sharks, they reproduce slowly and take years to reach sexual maturity. Madrigal-Mesén said that once the animals left Cocos Island, a volcanic island in the Pacific Ocean, and most monitored coastal sites, they entered waters with no protection, exposing them to threats including fishing and vessel traffic. "Studies like this help us recognise that these coastal havens only protect them for a specific time of the year. ... This is why it is so critical to protect the marine corridors these migratory species travel through." Coastal mantas also showed strong site fidelity, with very few moving between monitoring sites even when they were only tens of kilometres apart.  One male became a particularly striking example. Nicknamed "Mickey Mouse" for its distinctive spot pattern, the ray was repeatedly photographed at Cabo Blanco and tracked using both satellite and acoustic tags, showing a strong attachment to the site.  But researchers have not seen this ray in Costa Rica for more than a year.  "We have a lot of affection for him," Madrigal-Mesén added. "We hope he comes back soon."

FAST

NEW YORK, Oct 22 : The yen was on track for its strongest daily gain in almost a month on Thursday, as investors sought safety amid fragile equity markets, elevated crude prices from the drawn-out war in the Middle East, and doubts over future returns from artificial intelligence. The US dollar, meanwhile, rose against the euro. Worries about social unrest in France and a worsening fiscal outlook for the country outweighed concerns about the AI trade, which pushed US stocks lower. "AI is making people nervous, as is oil ... and as is France," said Chris Scicluna, head of economic research at Daiwa Capital Markets. Oil prices climbed about 3 per cent to a five-month high after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies from the key exporting region.

The Japanese yen strengthened 0.75 per cent to 156.96 per dollar. Some of the move in the yen may also be due to its approaching the key 160 level, which is seen as increasing the odds of further intervention by Japanese authorities to shore up the currency. Kevin Ford, lead FX and macro strategist at Convera, called it "the intervention premium," noting that "every time the yen gets closer to the 160 line, that's where there's higher speculation that the central bank will intervene." Against the Swiss franc, another traditional safe haven, the dollar weakened 0.42 per cent to  0.821 francs per dollar. The dollar index, which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.08 per cent to 101.60, with the euro down 0.09 per cent at $1.1222. The dollar has become increasingly tied to capital flows and to growth and inflation expectations linked to the AI trade. It fell last week as fears over the AI outlook grew. On Thursday, however, concerns about France outweighed those fears. "You have these competing stories and weak points between US AI-related credits and then France's sovereign credit, and we've seen this push and pull in the last couple of days where at times one is more of a concern than the other,” said Erik Nelson, global head of FX strategy at Wells Fargo. “As long as France is more of a concern than US AI credits, then you're going to see the euro underperform.” French President Emmanuel Macron said on Thursday that "illegitimate" protests would be banned in the coming days and blamed "seditious" ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's riots and looting. Concerns about France's ability to manage its huge debt burden have hurt French government bonds and raised worries about other heavily indebted euro zone countries. The spread between France and Germany's 10-year note yields reached 177.7 basis points on Thursday, the widest gap since 2011. Sterling strengthened 0.05 per cent to $1.3401. The Australian dollar  weakened 0.11 per cent to $0.7019. In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin fell 4.27 per cent to $81,023.  (Additional reporting by Amanda Cooper and Tom Westbrook; Editing by Xevi Fontdegloria and Andrea Ricci )

Source: Reuters

FAST

Oct 22 : The cost of insuring Meta Platforms' debt against default touched an all-time high on Thursday, as investors grappled with concerns about its plan to spend more on its AI build-out. Meta raised the lower end of its annual forecast for capital expenditure to between $135 billion and $145 billion this year, up from $130 billion to $145 billion expected previously. As a result, five-year credit default swaps widened 7.6 basis points to a record high of 114.79 bps and were set for its biggest one-day jump since at least 2025, Markit data showed. Its shares were last down 6.1 per cent at $655, hitting their lowest in about six weeks. Meta also introduced new non-voting shares and reported a free cash flow deficit of $2.12 billion in the third quarter, turning cash flow negative for the first time since 2012.

"The market has been questioning whether all the spending on AI is having the type of returns that the market originally expected," said Steve Sosnick, chief market analyst at Interactive Brokers. "In Meta's case, investors are interpreting the new non-voting shares as a backdoor for issuing more stock and diluting holdings eventually so I think that's adding to this aggressive selloff." Investors are growing more cautious about debt-fueled AI spending in the face of rising borrowing costs, with neocloud firm CoreWeave at the center of a storm that has erased more than 34 per cent of its market value this month. CoreWeave shares slumped 8.4 per cent on Thursday, while rival Nebius Group and data center operators IREN and Applied Digital also saw heavy losses. US chip stocks, widely viewed as one of the biggest winners of the AI boom, also sold off heavily with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index set to erase more than $688 billion in market value on Thursday alone. Five-year credit default swaps of hyperscaler Oracle were also close to a record high, while that of Amazon.com held near its highest level since March 2020, according to S&P Global Market Intelligence data. Oracle and Alphabet shares dropped more than 2 per cent, while Microsoft slipped 1.3 per cent and Amazon fell 3.7 per cent.
